new_statements.quote: Hay muy pocos lexemas que tienen un acento léxico. Normalmente cae en la penúltima sílaba, tal como muestran la realización del préstamo 'máscara' y los siguientes compuestos que han sido reinterpretados como un solo lexema: (8) máscara > maskára; cháyu ba > chayóba 'piña' + 'fruta madura' > 'piña'; báno do > banóro 'plátano maduro' + 'agua' > 'bebida de plátano raspado'.
new_statements.translation: Very few lexemes have a lexical accent. Normally it falls on the penultimate syllable, as shown by the realisation of the loanword 'máscara' and the following compounds, which have been reinterpreted as a single lexeme: (8) máscara > maskára; cháyu ba > chayóba 'pineapple' + 'ripe fruit' > 'pineapple'; báno do > banóro 'ripe plantain' + 'water' > 'drink of grated plantain'.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is regular on the penultimate syllable of the (lexical) word; Spanish loans with antepenultimate stress are regularised to penult (máscara > maskára) and univerbated compounds restress on the new penult (cháyu ba > chayóba). Only a handful of lexemes carry idiosyncratic (lexical) stress.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing said in the accessible text.
new_statements.exceptions: 'Muy pocos lexemas' have a lexically specified accent (not listed in the snippet).
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the lexeme/word (compounds reanalysed as one lexeme get a single penultimate stress); behaviour of stress under suffixation is not visible in the accessible snippet. Author notes (p.289) that the phonology is based on no more than ~1000 lexemes from semi-speakers/rememberers on the Mapiri river.
new_statements.identity_note: Source describes Leko as remembered by elderly semi-speakers on the Mapiri/Kaka river (Larecaja, La Paz), fieldwork 1994-2001; same language as Glottolog leco1242 / ISO lec (Lafone Quevedo's 'Leca/Lapalapa' of Atén/Apolo is the same language from 19th-c. mission documents). Not to be confused with Samba Leko / Chamba Leko (samb1305, Adamawa, Cameroon/Nigeria), which pollutes Glottolog's ref list (Fabre 2009).
